## formal
Work on the module $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{2})$ with the Majorana element $T = v_{1}\cdots v_{5}$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}), mass forms $B(\psi, X\varphi)$ on the sixteen with the pairing of Lemma \claimref{standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-modes}, the rung vectors $w_{4}$ (down-type) and $v_{4}$ (up-type), the $10$ form of $w_{4}$ and the Georgi-Jarlskog form of $w_{4}(B - L)\chi$ (Proposition \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}), and the pair part $P_{4} = \tfrac{3}{32}(B - L)(-1)^{N_{P}}$ of $TT^{\dagger}$, a $(15,1,1)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-is-rung-vector-times-pair-part-of-majorana-square}); and on the Pati-Salam route with the Clebsch structure of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw}, $M_{u} = \sum_{a}v_{u}^{a}Y_{a} + w_{u}f + c_{u}h$, $M_{\nu} = \sum_{a}v_{u}^{a}Y_{a} - 3w_{u}f + c_{\nu}h$, $M_{d} = \sum_{a}v_{d}^{a}Y_{a} + w_{d}f + c_{d}h$, $M_{e} = \sum_{a}v_{d}^{a}Y_{a} - 3w_{d}f + c_{e}h$, $M_{R} = v_{R}f$, $m_{\nu} = -M_{\nu}M_{R}^{-1}M_{\nu}^{\mathsf{T}}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Functions of the Majorana element.)} $T^{2} = (T^{\dagger})^{2} = 0$, $TT^{\dagger}T = T$ and $T^{\dagger}TT^{\dagger} = T^{\dagger}$, so $1, T, T^{\dagger}, TT^{\dagger}, T^{\dagger}T$ span the algebra generated by $T$ and $T^{\dagger}$. For every element $E$ of it the mass form of $w_{4}E$ is a multiple of the $10$ form (only $1$ contributes); for $v_{4}E$ the one further form, from $T^{\dagger}T$, has symmetric part half the $10$'s neutrino entry and no quark entry. So a coupling of the rung vector to operator functions of $T$ and $T^{\dagger}$ gives the down-type sector no Georgi-Jarlskog term: that term needs the $(15,1,1)$ projection of $TT^{\dagger}$, a linear map on its expansion in Majorana monomials, which the stored structure supplies and does not weight.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The weight moves the ratio.)} For numbers $a, b$, $w_{4}(a + bP_{4})$ gives the symmetric form with quark entries $a - \tfrac{b}{32}$ and lepton entries $a + \tfrac{3b}{32}$ in units of the $10$'s, and no antisymmetric part, so the lepton-to-quark ratio is $(32a + 3b)/(32a - b)$ (that the symmetric doublet forms span the $10$ and $T_{\mathrm{GJ}}$ forms with $y_{e}/y_{d}$ free is Proposition \claimref{standard-model.space-symmetric-doublet-mass-forms-two}; what is added here is the weight of $P_{4}$ and the Clebsch identification): $1$ at $b = 0$, $-3$ at $a = 0$, $+3$ at $b/a = \tfrac{32}{3}$. With $(a, b) = (v_{d}Y_{kk}, -32w_{d}f_{kk})$ on a family $k$ these are the down-type and charged-lepton entries $v_{d}Y + w_{d}f$ and $v_{d}Y - 3w_{d}f$ of the Clebsch structure without a $120$: the module weight $b/a$ is the $126$ coefficient relative to the $10$, $w_{d}f$ against $v_{d}Y$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(A symmetry of the stored relations.)} For real $\mu \neq 0$ let $h_{\mu}$ act on the Pati-Salam data by $w_{d} \mapsto \mu w_{d}$, all else fixed (composed, when the electroweak normalisation of the doublet vevs is imposed, with $(Y_{a}, v_{u}^{a}, v_{d}^{a}) \mapsto (Y_{a}/k, kv_{u}^{a}, kv_{d}^{a})$ on one $10$, which fixes every Dirac mass matrix). Then $M_{u}$, $M_{\nu}$, $M_{R}$ and $m_{\nu}$ are invariant; so are Premise (EW) (\claimref{standard-model.premise-ew-equal-weight}), $(M_{u})_{33} = m_{t} = 4w_{u}f_{33}$ with $(M_{\nu})_{33} = 0$ in its basis; the heavy-direction Majorana entry $(M_{R})_{33} = m_{t}v_{R}/(4w_{u})$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.majorana-scale-is-126-doublet-vev} and Premise \claimref{synthesis.majorana-scale-free-input}; without a $120$, $\hat{f} = \mathrm{Sym}(M_{d} - M_{e})/(M_{d} - M_{e})_{33} = f/f_{33}$ and $M_{\nu} = M_{u} - m_{t}\hat{f}$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.neutrino-dirac-matrix-charged-fermions}), hence Hypothesis (U) in both readings as Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hypothesis-u-under-ew-is-a-charged-fermion-condition}(i) states them, conditions on $\hat{f}$ with $m_{b}/m_{t}$ a given number; the chain and $v_{R}$; and the $S_{3}$- or $S_{2}$-invariance of every family matrix. The antisymmetric parts of the Dirac mass matrices are unchanged, and $\mathrm{Sym}(M_{d} - M_{e}) = 4\mu w_{d}f$. On the module $h_{\mu}$ is $b \mapsto \mu b$ in the down-type coupling of (ii).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Models.)} Let $v_{u} = v_{d} = w_{u} = 1$, $f = \mathrm{diag}(\tfrac{1}{10}, 1, 1)$ and $Y = \mathrm{diag}(-\tfrac{1}{10}, -1, 3)$, so that $M_{u} = \mathrm{diag}(0, 0, 4)$, $M_{\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-\tfrac25, -4, 0)$, (EW) holds exactly and $\sigma_{1}(M_{\nu}) = m_{t}$ (the top reading of (U)). Then $w_{d} = \tfrac13$ gives $(M_{e})_{22}/(M_{d})_{22} = 3$ and $w_{d} = \tfrac15$ gives $2$, with $M_{u}$, $M_{\nu}$, $M_{R}$ and $m_{\nu}$ equal; and $w_{d} = \tfrac15$ with $v_{d} = \tfrac{47}{45}$ gives $\tfrac{37}{19}$ with $\sigma_{1}(M_{d}) = (M_{d})_{33} = \tfrac{10}{3}$ equal to that of $w_{d} = \tfrac13$, $v_{d} = 1$, so the bottom reading of (U), read on the model's own $m_{b}$, fails in both ($\sigma_{1}(N) = 1$ against $m_{b}/m_{t} = \tfrac56$) and does not separate them. The diagonal model satisfies every postulate of the cone and of the relations audited: (EW), (U) in its eigenvalue (top) reading, Premise (H) ($m_{\nu}$ has the eigenvalue $0$), Premise (M) ($v_{R} = 1000$ against doublet vevs of $1$), the real-breaking assumption (all data real), the face identification and the indifference premise, which speak of no coupling weight; so a model of all of them with $w_{d}f \neq 0$ exists, as the invariance under $h_{\mu}$ requires. With an $S_{3}$-invariant Majorana matrix, $f = (\alpha\Pi + M_{3}\J/3)/v_{R}$, $\mathrm{Sym}(M_{d} - M_{e}) = 4\mu w_{d}f$ stays $S_{3}$-invariant and its light-plane value $4\mu w_{d}\alpha/v_{R}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residual-s2-fixes-120-family-form}(iii)) moves with $\mu$.
\end{enumerate}
Premise (EW) and Hypothesis (U) are not premises of this result: no step assumes them; they are relations the models are shown to satisfy, which is what an independence proof needs. (U) is satisfied in its eigenvalue (top) reading, in which Theorem \claimref{synthesis.hypothesis-u-under-ew-is-a-charged-fermion-condition} shows it consistent with (EW); the store's contradicts link between (U) and (EW) concerns the entry reading $(M_{\nu})_{33} = m_{t}$, and taking both as premises would carry it.
So no stored relation fixes the $126$ coefficient relative to the $10$ in the down-type sector, on the Majorana route (the weight $b/a$) or on the Pati-Salam route ($w_{d}f$ against $v_{d}Y$): the relations determine it only through the down-quark and charged-lepton matrices, $\mathrm{Sym}(M_{d} - M_{e}) = 4w_{d}f$, so the second family's factor $3$ is an input taken from the record, and with it $m_{b}/m_{\tau}$ at $M_{I}$. Premise (EW) fixes a $126$-to-$10$ ratio only in the up sector along the heavy direction, $v_{u}Y_{33} = 3w_{u}f_{33}$ in its basis.

## technical
The open number of the problem, the weight of the $(15,1,1)$ part of the Majorana square against the rung vector's $10$ term, is shown to be unconstrained by every relation the store holds. First, a coupling through functions of the Majorana element itself cannot produce it: $T$ and $T^{\dagger}$ generate a five-dimensional algebra, and the down-type rung vector times any element of it gives a multiple of the $10$ form, so the Georgi-Jarlskog form appears only after projecting the square on a Pati-Salam component. Second, the weight $b/a$ of that projection sets the lepton-to-quark ratio of the down-type form as $(32a + 3b)/(32a - b)$, and on each family it is exactly the Clebsch structure's $w_{d}f$ against $v_{d}Y$.

Third, scaling the $126$'s down-type doublet admixture $w_{d}$ alone leaves the up and neutrino Dirac mass matrices, the Majorana matrix, the light neutrino matrix, Premise (EW), the Majorana scale premise, the neutrino Dirac mass matrix under (EW) and with it Hypothesis (U) in its eigenvalue readings (with $m_{b}/m_{t}$ given; models satisfy the top reading), the chain and the family symmetries unchanged, and multiplies the symmetric part of $M_{d} - M_{e}$ by the same factor. The stored Majorana scaling moves $w_{u}$ and $w_{d}$ together against $f$ and so fixes $w_{d}f$; this one moves $w_{d}$ alone. Exact models with the same up, neutrino and Majorana sectors have second-family factors $3$, $2$ and $\tfrac{37}{19}$, the last at the same bottom mass. So the factor $3$ is not derived: it is read from the measured masses. The check verifies all four clauses exactly, on the $32$-dimensional module and on two family-matrix models (one diagonal, one with off-diagonal entries and a $120$) for four values of $\mu$.

## lay
In the version of the theory where quarks and leptons are unified, the mass of the strange quark and of the muon come from two kinds of Higgs field: one gives them equal masses, the other gives the muon three times the strange quark's mass, which is what the measurements suggest at very high energies. How much of each kind enters is a number. This result shows that nothing the theory has stored fixes that number. A coupling built from the theory's heavy-neutrino element alone gives only the equal-mass kind. Changing the weight of the second kind, through one unmeasured Higgs mixing, leaves every stored relation true, including the assumptions about the heavy neutrino and the top quark. Only the masses of the down-type quarks and the charged leptons change. So the factor three is taken from the data, not predicted.

## one-liner
Operator functions of the Majorana element give the down-type rung vector only the $10$; the $(15,1,1)$ weight $b/a$ sets $m_{\mu}/m_{s}$ as $(32a + 3b)/(32a - b)$ and is $w_{d}f$ against $v_{d}Y$; $w_{d} \mapsto \mu w_{d}$ fixes every stored relation ((EW), the Majorana scale, (U) in its eigenvalue reading, the chain) and moves $\mathrm{Sym}(M_{d} - M_{e})$ by $\mu$, so the second family's factor $3$ is an input.
check_py:
"""synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-weight-free-on-the-stored-relations: exact checks.

Module part: the five-mode module Lambda(W + R_2) as 32 x 32 rational matrices (fock.py, LSB order), modes 0, 1, 2
the pairs, 3, 4 the rungs, as in the stored checks of the Majorana element's square; T = v_1 ... v_5; the pair part
of the square P_4 = (3/32)(B - L)(-1)^{N_P} (stored identity); mass forms B(psi, X phi) on the sixteen with the
stored pairing. Pati-Salam part: 3 x 3 rational family matrices with the imported Clebsch structure
M_u = v_u Y + w_u f + c_u h, M_nu = v_u Y - 3 w_u f + c_nu h, M_d = v_d Y + w_d f + c_d h,
M_e = v_d Y - 3 w_d f + c_e h, M_R = v_R f, m_nu = -M_nu M_R^{-1} M_nu^T; h_mu: w_d -> mu w_d.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations, permutations

import GA
import fock
from tp_premise import premise

NM = 5
STATES = [s for k in range(NM + 1) for s in combinations(range(NM), k)]
IDX = {s: sum(1 << x for x in s) for s in STATES}
STATE_OF = {i: s for s, i in IDX.items()}
D = len(STATES)
mm, madd, msc, tr, comm = fock.mm, fock.madd, fock.msc, fock.transpose, fock.comm
PAIRS = (0, 1, 2)
SIXTEEN = [s for s in STATES if len(s) % 2 == 0]


def nw(s):
    return sum(1 for x in s if x in PAIRS)


def nr(s):
    return sum(1 for x in s if x not in PAIRS)


def diag(fn):
    return fock.diag(lambda i: fn(STATE_OF[i]), D)


V = [fock.cre(k, NM) for k in range(NM)]
W = [tr(v) for v in V]
ONE = fock.eye(D)
BL = diag(lambda s: 1 - F(2, 3) * nw(s))
CHI = diag(lambda s: -(-1) ** nr(s))
PPAR = diag(lambda s: (-1) ** nw(s))
P4 = msc(F(3, 32), mm(BL, PPAR))
T = mm(mm(mm(mm(V[0], V[1]), V[2]), V[3]), V[4])
TD = tr(T)
W4, V4 = W[3], V[3]

BMAT = {}
for s in STATES:
    comp = tuple(x for x in range(NM) if x not in s)
    seq = list(s) + list(comp)
    inv = sum(1 for i in range(NM) for j in range(i + 1, NM) if seq[i] > seq[j])
    k = len(s)
    BMAT[(IDX[s], IDX[comp])] = F((-1) ** (k * (k - 1) // 2) * (-1) ** inv)


def forms(X):
    """symmetric and antisymmetric parts of B(psi, X phi) on the sixteen."""
    BX = mm(BMAT, X)
    sym, anti = {}, {}
    for a in SIXTEEN:
        for b in SIXTEEN:
            x, y = BX.get((IDX[a], IDX[b]), 0), BX.get((IDX[b], IDX[a]), 0)
            if x + y:
                sym[(a, b)] = (x + y) * F(1, 2)
            if x - y:
                anti[(a, b)] = (x - y) * F(1, 2)
    return sym, anti


def is_multiple(f, g):
    c = None
    for k in set(f) | set(g):
        a, b = f.get(k, F(0)), g.get(k, F(0))
        if b == 0:
            if a != 0:
                return None
            continue
        if c is None:
            c = a / b
        elif a != c * b:
            return None
    return c if c is not None else F(0)


S10, A10 = forms(W4)
SGJ, _ = forms(mm(mm(W4, BL), CHI))
LEP = [k for k in S10 if nw(k[0]) in (0, 3)]
QRK = [k for k in S10 if nw(k[0]) in (1, 2)]


def entries(sym):
    """(quark entry, lepton entry) of a symmetric rung form, relative to the 10 form's entries."""
    q = {sym.get(k, F(0)) / S10[k] for k in QRK}
    l = {sym.get(k, F(0)) / S10[k] for k in LEP}
    if len(q) != 1 or len(l) != 1 or set(sym) - set(S10):
        return None
    return q.pop(), l.pop()


def check_operator_functions_of_the_majorana_element_give_only_the_ten():
    """(i) T^2 = 0, (T^dag)^2 = 0, T T^dag T = T, T^dag T T^dag = T^dag, so 1, T, T^dag, T T^dag, T^dag T span the
    algebra they generate; with the down-type rung vector w_4 only 1 gives a mass form on the sixteen, the 10 form,
    so every operator function of T and T^dag gives w_4 a multiple of the 10, never the GJ form; with v_4 the one
    further form, from T^dag T, is half the 10's neutrino entry (plus an antisymmetric part), with no quark entry."""
    premise("standard-model.majorana-element")
    premise("standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-modes")
    premise("synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-square-of-majorana-element")
    TT, DT = mm(T, TD), mm(TD, T)
    GA.check("T^2 = 0", mm(T, T) == {})
    GA.check("Tdag^2 = 0", mm(TD, TD) == {})
    GA.check("T Tdag T = T", mm(TT, T) == T)
    GA.check("Tdag T Tdag = Tdag", mm(DT, TD) == TD)
    basis = [T, TD, TT, DT]
    prods = [mm(x, y) for x in basis for y in basis]
    span = [ONE, T, TD, TT, DT]
    GA.check("products stay in the span", all(p == {} or any(p == s or p == msc(F(-1), s) for s in span) for p in prods))
    GA.check("10 form nonzero, symmetric", S10 != {} and A10 == {})
    for E in basis:
        s, a = forms(mm(W4, E))
        GA.check("w_4 E: no mass form for E = T, Tdag, T Tdag, Tdag T", s == {} and a == {})
    for E in (T, TD, TT):
        s, a = forms(mm(V4, E))
        GA.check("v_4 E: no mass form for E = T, Tdag, T Tdag", s == {} and a == {})
    S10u, _ = forms(V4)
    s, a = forms(mm(V4, DT))
    nu = {k: v for k, v in S10u.items() if k[0] == () or k[1] == ()}
    GA.check("v_4 Tdag T: symmetric part half the 10's neutrino entry, no quark entry, an antisymmetric part",
             is_multiple(s, nu) == F(1, 2) and len(nu) == 2 and a != {})
    GA.check("the GJ form is not a multiple of the 10", is_multiple(SGJ, S10) is None)
    return True


WEIGHTS = ((F(1), F(0), F(1)), (F(0), F(1), F(-3)), (F(3), F(32), F(3)), (F(1), F(16), F(5)),
           (F(2), F(-5), F(49, 69)))


def check_weighting_of_the_pair_part_moves_the_lepton_quark_ratio():
    """(ii) w_4 (a + b P_4) gives the symmetric form with quark entries a - b/32 and lepton entries a + 3b/32 (relative
    to the 10's), no antisymmetric part, P_4 commuting with B - L and the rung parity (its Pati-Salam type is stored); the ratio is
    (32a + 3b)/(32a - b): 1 at b = 0, -3 at a = 0, +3 at b/a = 32/3; with (a, b) = (v_d Y_kk, -32 w_d f_kk) the
    entries are v_d Y + w_d f and v_d Y - 3 w_d f, the down-type and lepton entries of the imported Clebsch structure."""
    premise("synthesis.georgi-jarlskog-is-rung-vector-times-pair-part-of-majorana-square")
    premise("families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch")
    premise("standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw")
    GA.check("P_4 commutes with B - L and the rung parity, not with the pair bracket",
             comm(P4, BL) == {} and comm(P4, CHI) == {} and comm(P4, mm(V[0], V[1])) != {})
    for a, b, ratio in WEIGHTS:
        s, an = forms(mm(W4, madd(msc(a, ONE), msc(b, P4))))
        e = entries(s)
        GA.check("no antisymmetric part", an == {})
        GA.check("quark a - b/32, lepton a + 3b/32", e == (a - b / 32, a + 3 * b / 32))
        GA.check("lepton/quark ratio (32a + 3b)/(32a - b)", e[1] / e[0] == ratio == (32 * a + 3 * b) / (32 * a - b))
    for vd, Ykk, wd, fkk, expect in ((F(1), F(-1), F(1, 3), F(1), (F(-2, 3), F(-2))),
                                     (F(1, 2), F(3), F(-2), F(1, 7), (F(17, 14), F(33, 14)))):
        s, _ = forms(mm(W4, madd(msc(vd * Ykk, ONE), msc(-32 * wd * fkk, P4))))
        GA.check("module coupling realises the Clebsch down and lepton entries",
                 entries(s) == (vd * Ykk + wd * fkk, vd * Ykk - 3 * wd * fkk) == expect)
    return True


def mat(rows):
    return [[F(x) for x in r] for r in rows]


def mmul(A, B):
    return [[sum((A[i][k] * B[k][j] for k in range(3)), F(0)) for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]


def madd3(*args):
    out = [[F(0)] * 3 for _ in range(3)]
    for c, A in args:
        out = [[out[i][j] + c * A[i][j] for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
    return out


def tp3(A):
    return [[A[j][i] for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]


def inv3(A):
    a = A
    det = (a[0][0] * (a[1][1] * a[2][2] - a[1][2] * a[2][1]) - a[0][1] * (a[1][0] * a[2][2] - a[1][2] * a[2][0])
           + a[0][2] * (a[1][0] * a[2][1] - a[1][1] * a[2][0]))
    cof = [[(a[(j + 1) % 3][(i + 1) % 3] * a[(j + 2) % 3][(i + 2) % 3]
             - a[(j + 1) % 3][(i + 2) % 3] * a[(j + 2) % 3][(i + 1) % 3]) for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]
    return [[cof[i][j] / det for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)]


def sym(A):
    return madd3((F(1, 2), A), (F(1, 2), tp3(A)))


E33 = mat([[0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1]])


def masses(d, mu):
    Y, f, h = d["Y"], d["f"], d["h"]
    vu, vd, wu, wd, vR = d["vu"], d["vd"], d["wu"], mu * d["wd"], d["vR"]
    cu, cn, cd, ce = d["c"]
    Mu = madd3((vu, Y), (wu, f), (cu, h))
    Mn = madd3((vu, Y), (-3 * wu, f), (cn, h))
    Md = madd3((vd, Y), (wd, f), (cd, h))
    Me = madd3((vd, Y), (-3 * wd, f), (ce, h))
    MR = madd3((vR, f))
    mnu = madd3((F(-1), mmul(mmul(Mn, inv3(MR)), tp3(Mn))))
    return Mu, Mn, Md, Me, MR, mnu


# diagonal model: v_u = v_d = w_u = 1, f = diag(1/10, 1, 1), M_u = diag(0, 0, 4), (EW) exact
DIAG = {"Y": mat([[F(-1, 10), 0, 0], [0, -1, 0], [0, 0, 3]]), "f": mat([[F(1, 10), 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]),
        "h": mat([[0] * 3] * 3), "vu": F(1), "vd": F(1), "wu": F(1), "wd": F(1, 3), "vR": F(1000),
        "c": (F(0), F(0), F(0), F(0))}
# general model: symmetric f with off-diagonal entries, a 120, M_u = diag(1/1000, 1/10, 4) in the (EW) basis
F_GEN = mat([[F(1, 10), F(1, 20), 0], [F(1, 20), 1, F(1, 5)], [0, F(1, 5), 1]])
H_GEN = mat([[0, F(1, 50), F(-1, 30)], [F(-1, 50), 0, F(1, 40)], [F(1, 30), F(-1, 40), 0]])
MU_GEN = mat([[F(1, 1000), 0, 0], [0, F(1, 10), 0], [0, 0, 4]])
GEN = {"Y": madd3((F(1), MU_GEN), (F(-1), F_GEN), (F(-1, 2), H_GEN)), "f": F_GEN, "h": H_GEN,
       "vu": F(1), "vd": F(1, 2), "wu": F(1), "wd": F(1, 4), "vR": F(5000), "c": (F(1, 2), F(-3, 2), F(2), F(-1))}
MUS = (F(1), F(3, 5), F(-2), F(7, 3))


def check_h_mu_fixes_every_stored_relation_and_moves_the_down_type_126():
    """(iii) Under h_mu (w_d -> mu w_d, mu nonzero): M_u, M_nu, M_R and m_nu are unchanged; Premise (EW)
    (M_u)_33 = m_t = 4 w_u f_33 and (M_nu)_33 = 0 holds; the Majorana scale (M_R)_33 = m_t v_R/(4 w_u) holds;
    f-hat = Sym(M_d - M_e)/(M_d - M_e)_33 = f/f_33 is unchanged (no 120), so is M_nu = M_u - m_t f-hat;
    Sym(M_d - M_e) = 4 mu w_d f and Sym(M_u - M_nu) = 4 w_u f; the antisymmetric parts are untouched; composing
    with (Y, v_u, v_d) -> (Y/k, k v_u, k v_d) fixes every Dirac matrix (electroweak normalisation)."""
    premise("standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw")
    premise("synthesis.majorana-scale-is-126-doublet-vev")
    premise("standard-model.neutrino-dirac-matrix-charged-fermions")
    premise("synthesis.hypothesis-u-under-ew-is-a-charged-fermion-condition")
    premise("standard-model.imported-spinor-bilinears")
    for d in (DIAG, GEN):
        Mu0, Mn0, Md0, Me0, MR0, mn0 = masses(d, F(1))
        mt = Mu0[2][2]
        GA.check("Sym M_u diagonal in the (EW) basis", all(sym(Mu0)[i][j] == 0 for i in range(3) for j in range(3) if i != j))
        for mu in MUS:
            Mu, Mn, Md, Me, MR, mnu = masses(d, mu)
            GA.check("M_u, M_nu, M_R, m_nu unchanged", (Mu, Mn, MR, mnu) == (Mu0, Mn0, MR0, mn0))
            GA.check("(EW): (M_nu)_33 = 0 and m_t = 4 w_u f_33", Mn[2][2] == 0 and mt == 4 * d["wu"] * d["f"][2][2])
            GA.check("Majorana scale (M_R)_33 = m_t v_R/(4 w_u)", MR[2][2] == mt * d["vR"] / (4 * d["wu"]))
            GA.check("Sym(M_d - M_e) = 4 mu w_d f", sym(madd3((F(1), Md), (F(-1), Me))) == madd3((4 * mu * d["wd"], d["f"])))
            GA.check("Sym(M_u - M_nu) = 4 w_u f", sym(madd3((F(1), Mu), (F(-1), Mn))) == madd3((4 * d["wu"], d["f"])))
            GA.check("antisymmetric parts of M_d - M_e unchanged",
                     madd3((F(1), Md), (F(-1), Me), (F(-1), sym(madd3((F(1), Md), (F(-1), Me))))) ==
                     madd3((F(1), Md0), (F(-1), Me0), (F(-1), sym(madd3((F(1), Md0), (F(-1), Me0))))))
            if d is DIAG:
                dm = madd3((F(1), Md), (F(-1), Me))
                fhat = madd3((1 / dm[2][2], dm))
                GA.check("f-hat = f/f_33 unchanged", fhat == madd3((1 / d["f"][2][2], d["f"])))
                GA.check("M_nu = M_u - m_t f-hat", Mn == madd3((F(1), Mu), (-mt, fhat)))
            k = F(2)
            d2 = dict(d, Y=madd3((1 / k, d["Y"])), vu=k * d["vu"], vd=k * d["vd"])
            GA.check("10 rescaling fixes every Dirac matrix", masses(d2, mu)[:4] == (Mu, Mn, Md, Me))
        GA.check("M_d moves", masses(d, F(3, 5))[2] != Md0)
    return True


PERMS = [[[F(1) if p[i] == j else F(0) for j in range(3)] for i in range(3)] for p in permutations(range(3))]


def check_two_models_of_the_premises_differ_in_the_second_family_factor():
    """(iv) In the diagonal model, w_d = 1/3 gives m_mu/m_s = (M_e)_22/(M_d)_22 = 3 and w_d = 1/5 gives 2, with M_u,
    M_nu (singular values 2/5, 4, 0, so the top reading of (U), sigma_1(M_nu) = m_t), M_R, m_nu, (EW) and the
    Majorana scale identical; w_d = 1/5 with v_d = 47/45 gives 37/19 at the same bottom mass sigma_1(M_d) = 10/3 as
    w_d = 1/3, v_d = 1 (the bottom reading of (U) on the model's own m_b fails in both, sigma_1(N) = 1 against m_b/m_t = 5/6); the diagonal
    model satisfies (H) (m_nu = -diag(1/625, 2/125, 0)) and (M) (v_R = 1000); with an S_3-invariant Majorana matrix (f = alpha Pi + M_3 J/3) Sym(M_d - M_e) =
    4 mu w_d f stays S_3-invariant and its light-plane value 4 mu w_d alpha moves with mu."""
    premise("standard-model.imported-clebsch-structure-seesaw")
    premise("synthesis.residual-s2-fixes-120-family-form")
    premise("neutrino.breaking-relation")
    A = masses(DIAG, F(1))
    B = masses(DIAG, F(3, 5))
    GA.check("model A: second-family factor 3", A[3][1][1] / A[2][1][1] == 3)
    GA.check("model B: second-family factor 2", B[3][1][1] / B[2][1][1] == 2)
    GA.check("the 126 down-type weight differs", A[2][1][1] - B[2][1][1] == F(2, 15))
    GA.check("same M_u, M_nu, M_R, m_nu", A[0] == B[0] and A[1] == B[1] and A[4] == B[4] and A[5] == B[5])
    GA.check("M_nu = diag(-2/5, -4, 0): top reading sigma_1 = m_t", A[1] == mat([[F(-2, 5), 0, 0], [0, -4, 0], [0, 0, 0]])
             and A[0][2][2] == 4)
    C = masses(dict(DIAG, vd=F(47, 45)), F(3, 5))
    GA.check("model C: factor 37/19 at the same bottom mass 10/3",
             C[3][1][1] / C[2][1][1] == F(37, 19) and C[2][2][2] == A[2][2][2] == F(10, 3)
             and all(abs(X[2][i][i]) < X[2][2][2] for X in (A, C) for i in range(2)))
    GA.check("model C: same M_u, M_nu, M_R, m_nu", C[0] == A[0] and C[1] == A[1] and C[4] == A[4] and C[5] == A[5])
    GA.check("(H): m_nu = -diag(1/625, 2/125, 0), the lightest massless, in A, B and C",
             A[5] == B[5] == C[5] == mat([[F(-1, 625), 0, 0], [0, F(-2, 125), 0], [0, 0, 0]]))
    GA.check("(M): Majorana term at v_R = 1000, M_R = diag(100, 1000, 1000)", A[4] == mat([[100, 0, 0], [0, 1000, 0], [0, 0, 1000]]))
    Nm = madd3((F(1), DIAG["f"]), (F(-1), E33))
    GA.check("bottom reading fails in A and C: sigma_1(N) = 1, m_b/m_t = 5/6",
             max(abs(Nm[i][i]) for i in range(3)) == 1 and A[2][2][2] / A[0][2][2] == C[2][2][2] / C[0][2][2] == F(5, 6))
    J = mat([[1] * 3] * 3)
    PI = madd3((F(1), mat([[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]])), (F(-1, 3), J))
    alpha, M3 = F(2, 7), F(5)
    fS = madd3((alpha, PI), (M3 / 3, J))
    u = [F(1), F(-1), F(0)]
    for mu in MUS:
        dS = madd3((4 * mu * F(1, 3), fS))
        GA.check("S_3-invariant", all(mmul(mmul(P, dS), tp3(P)) == dS for P in PERMS))
        GA.check("light-plane value 4 mu w_d alpha",
                 [sum((dS[i][j] * u[j] for j in range(3)), F(0)) for i in range(3)] == [4 * mu * F(1, 3) * alpha * x for x in u])
    return True
